basis: Only the two actual canonical PNG pixel views; no author report, author inventory, candidate spec, SVG, render report, or candidate preview was read before this inventory.

figures.frame: One shared planar ray diagram; horizontal principal axis through O, F, and mirror pole P. No grid, axes with ticks, dimensional annotations, angle values, or subpanels.

pointsAndLabels.label: O
pointsAndLabels.pixelFact: Filled round point on the principal axis at the far left, with O above-left of it.

pointsAndLabels.label: F
pointsAndLabels.pixelFact: Dark common convergence on the axis between O and the mirror, with F above the junction.

pointsAndLabels.label: P
pointsAndLabels.pixelFact: Mirror-axis intersection at the right; P is printed immediately left of the mirror and above the axis. No separately distinguishable point marker at P.

figures.mirror: A curved vertical concave reflecting surface on the right faces left. Its upper and lower ends extend farther left than its central pole. Short diagonal hatch marks are on its right/back side throughout the mirror height.

rays.incident: Top horizontal solid ray from left to upper mirror contact, with a right-pointing arrowhead.
rays.reflected: Solid contact-to-F line continues down-left past F, with a down-left arrowhead.

rays.incident: Second horizontal solid ray from left to upper-middle contact, with a right-pointing arrowhead.
rays.reflected: Solid contact-to-F line continues down-left past F, with a down-left arrowhead.

rays.incident: Third horizontal solid ray from left to upper-inner contact, with a right-pointing arrowhead.
rays.reflected: Solid contact-to-F line continues gently down-left past F, with a left/down-left arrowhead.

rays.incident: First solid horizontal ray below the axis from left to lower-inner contact, with a right-pointing arrowhead.
rays.reflected: Solid contact-to-F line continues gently up-left past F, with a left/up-left arrowhead.

rays.incident: Second solid horizontal ray below the axis from left to lower-middle contact, with a right-pointing arrowhead.
rays.reflected: Solid contact-to-F line continues up-left past F, with an up-left arrowhead.

rays.incident: Bottom solid horizontal ray from left to lower mirror contact, with a right-pointing arrowhead.
rays.reflected: Solid contact-to-F line continues up-left past F, with an up-left arrowhead.

countsAndRelationships: Six off-axis incident rays: three above and three below the principal axis; six distinct mirror contacts and six reflected branches.
Six rightward incident arrowheads and six leftward reflected arrowheads are visibly distinguishable.
All incident rays are parallel to the principal axis; all six reflected lines meet at the same F on that axis.
Left-to-right axial order is O, F, P. F appears approximately midway between O and P; the source gives no numerical measurement.
The principal axis is a solid horizontal line, not an additional arrowed incident ray.
All ray segments are solid. There are no dashed constructions.
The black original figure number 143 is beneath the diagram; it is not a mathematical given.
figures.sourceUncertainty: The convergence is ink-heavy, and the six outgoing branches must be counted away from F. No exact incidence/reflection angle equality or exact spherical geometry can be measured reliably from this raster.

figures.frame: One shared planar ray diagram. A horizontal solid principal axis crosses a vertical dashed focal-plane line at F. The concave mirror is on the right. No grid, numerical scale, angle annotation, or subpanel.

pointsAndLabels.label: O
pointsAndLabels.pixelFact: Small open circular point on the principal axis to the left of F; O is above-left of that point.

pointsAndLabels.label: F
pointsAndLabels.pixelFact: Small open circular point at the dashed focal plane/principal-axis intersection; F is above-left of it.

pointsAndLabels.label: D
pointsAndLabels.pixelFact: Dark common ray junction on the dashed focal-plane line above F; D is above-right of that junction.

pointsAndLabels.label: C
pointsAndLabels.pixelFact: Uppermost ray contact on the upper mirror portion; C is left of the contact.

pointsAndLabels.label: K
pointsAndLabels.pixelFact: Second ray contact down the mirror, at the level of D; K is above-left of it.

pointsAndLabels.label: P
pointsAndLabels.pixelFact: Third ray contact, coinciding with the mirror pole on the principal axis; P is above-left of it.
Fourth ray contact on the mirror below the principal axis; no letter is printed for this contact.

figures.mirror: Curved upright concave mirror faces left, with upper and lower ends left of the central pole. Diagonal backing hatch marks are on its right side, not on the reflecting left face.
figures.focalPlane: One vertical dashed line through F and D, extending substantially above D and below F. A vertically set non-English source label reads focal plane; modern output should translate it into English rather than copy the source characters.

rays.incident: Solid oblique line rises from lower-left through O and D toward C, with a right/up-right arrowhead between O and D.
rays.reflected: The C-to-D solid segment continues left/down-left past D on the same visible line, with a down-left arrowhead beyond O.

rays.incident: Second solid line parallel to the first rises from lower-left through F toward K, with a right/up-right arrowhead left of F.
rays.reflected: Solid horizontal K-to-D line continues leftward through D, with a left-pointing arrowhead.

rays.incident: Third solid parallel line rises from lower-left to P, with a right/up-right arrowhead left of the focal plane.
rays.reflected: Solid P-to-D line continues up-left beyond D, with an up-left arrowhead.

rays.incident: Fourth solid parallel line rises from lower-left to the unlabeled lower contact, with a right/up-right arrowhead left of the focal plane.
rays.reflected: Solid lower-contact-to-D line continues up-left beyond D, with an up-left arrowhead.

countsAndRelationships: Four parallel oblique incident rays and four reflected rays; four contacts ordered C, K, P, unlabeled lower contact from top to bottom.
Four right/up-right incident arrowheads and four leftward reflected arrowheads are visibly distinguishable.
All four reflected lines share D above F on the dashed focal plane.
The top incident/reflected line passes through O, D, C. The second incident line passes through F and K. The K-D reflected segment is horizontal.
Principal-axis point order is O, F, P. D is vertically above F and K is to the right of D.
The ray through P reaches the mirror on the principal axis. The lowest mirror contact is deliberately unlabeled.
The principal axis has no arrowhead. Ray lines are solid; the focal plane alone is dashed.
The original figure number 144 is below the diagram. There are no lengths, units, plus/minus signs, or answer values.
figures.sourceUncertainty: The old drawing uses a visibly wide oblique bundle. Pixel topology, shared contacts, and arrow direction are evidence; exact spherical ray-law accuracy is not. Any modern idealization must be distinguished from source facts and stay within the lesson's paraxial approximation.
